description: Liveline is a real-time line chart control for Uno Platform, drawn with SkiaSharp on an SKCanvasElement. The sample shows one chart on a live feed: a short loading state, then a volatile random walk with a new value every 150 ms. The line, its gradient fill, the value range and the badge ease toward each new value, a live dot marks the latest value, and the chart stops drawing once the line settles. Its default style binds every colour to the Material palette's roles, so the chart follows Light, Dark and any palette with no wiring.

messages.content: Liveline is built and running: the chart loads for three seconds, then follows a live random walk and settles between updates.

messages.content: This is Liveline, a real-time animated line chart control for Uno Platform, shown on a live random-walk feed.

Liveline is one Uno single project, `Liveline.Demo/Liveline.Demo.csproj` (Uno.Sdk from `global.json`, heads net10.0-desktop and net10.0-browserwasm, UnoFeatures Material, Toolkit, Skia, SkiaRenderer). The chart control lives in the project's `Liveline/` folder with its default style in `Themes/Generic.xaml`; the page is the demo.

Theming: `App.xaml` merges `MaterialToolkitTheme` with one brand seed (`<ut:ThemeColors PrimarySeed="#4CAF50" />`) and the chart's `Themes/Generic.xaml` (an app project must merge it; a library loads it by itself). No colour, corner or spacing value is defined anywhere else: pages and the control use palette role brushes (`{ThemeResource PrimaryBrush}`…), `Radius*CornerRadius` and `Space*Thickness` tokens. Keep it that way: to rebrand, change the seed or add a palette override on the theme's `Colors`; never put a hex colour in a page, style or C#.

Key files:
- `MainPage.xaml`: a single `liveline:LivelineChart` named `Chart` inside an outlined card (`Border` with `Radius400CornerRadius`, `OutlineVariantBrush`, a `ThemeShadow`), at most 720 wide, 280 high on a phone and 360 from 600 wide (`utu:Responsive`), centred in a Toolkit `SafeArea` grid on `BackgroundBrush`.
- `MainPage.xaml.cs`: the feed. It sets `IsLoading`, waits 3 s on a `DispatcherTimer`, seeds 60 points, then adds a random-walk value every 150 ms (with an 8% chance of a spike), keeps the last 60 points, and sets `Chart.Data` and `Chart.Value`.
- `Liveline/LivelineChart.cs`: the public templated `Control` (template part `PART_Canvas`). Dependency properties: `Data`, `Value`, `ShowGrid`, `ShowBadge`, `ShowFill`, `ShowTrackingLine`, `Momentum`, `LerpSpeed`, `IsLoading`, `IsPaused`, `WindowStart`/`WindowEnd`/`NowTime`, `Forecast`/`ForecastOpacity`, brushes (`ChartBackground`, `LineBrush`, `FillTopBrush`, `FillBottomBrush`, `GridLineBrush`, `LabelBrush`, `BadgeTextBrush`, `LabelHaloBrush`; the default style binds them to `SurfaceBrush`, `PrimaryBrush`, `OutlineVariantBrush`, `OnSurfaceVariantBrush`, `OnPrimaryBrush`, and the fill derives from the line), `StrokeThickness`, `PlotPadding`, `ValueMin`/`ValueMax`, `Typeface` and `Markers`. Every property change pushes one immutable state to the canvas.
- `Liveline/LivelineChartCanvas.cs`: an `SKCanvasElement` that draws the frame with the renderers in `Liveline/Rendering/` (grid, line and fill, badge, markers, and the live dot that `Momentum` turns on) over a `RenderContext`.
- `Liveline/Animation/LerpEngine.cs`: per-frame easing (by `LerpSpeed`) of the line, the value range and the badge toward their targets.
- `Liveline/Models/`: `LivelinePoint` (time, value), `LivelineMarker` (colours left null follow the chart), `MomentumDirection`. `Helpers/ColorHelper.cs` holds the per-frame `ChartPalette`, read from the brushes.
- `Themes/Generic.xaml`: the chart's default style: template and theme brushes. A theme change re-resolves the setters, the brush properties change and the chart redraws.

Animation: the control subscribes to `CompositionTarget.Rendering` while the line is moving and unsubscribes as soon as `TickAnimation()` reports it has settled; the next property change re-attaches. Keep that: a held Rendering subscription makes the compositor draw at display refresh for nothing. Allocate paints and paths outside the per-frame path.

The page uses code-behind on purpose: the feed is a timer, and there is no navigation, MVUX or MVVM. Data is simulated; nothing leaves the device.

Build: `dotnet build Liveline.Demo/Liveline.Demo.csproj -f net10.0-desktop`, or `-f net10.0-browserwasm` for WebAssembly. There are no tests.

The app is built and running. The user may ask me to modify it.
